subject: Eval credits proposal for Brightly Health RFP
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@brightlyhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Brightly RFP bake-off — request for evaluation credits and timing

Hi Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency and the cost breakdowns. We are running a tight bake-off timeline and will be evaluating three vendors the week of May 22.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood provide evaluation credits to cover a 2-week benchmark (estimated ~120k tokens)?
- Would you be able to extend the trial window for our engineers until June 5 so SRE can run longer context tests?
- We’d also like a short credit/usage agreement that our procurement team can attach to the RFP.

We’re trying to keep parity with what Vendor X is offering for the bake-off. If Redwood can match the credit amount and provide a short MSA amendment for evaluation only, procurement can expedite vendor scoring.

Looping procurement (procurement@brightlyhealth.com) and SRE (sre@brightlyhealth.com).

Thanks,
Asha Patel
Director, Applied ML
Brightly Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@brightlyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightly RFP bake-off — request for evaluation credits and timing

Asha — appreciate the clear scope. We’d be happy to support the bake-off. Here’s an internal-proposed structure (subject to quick approvals from my finance and sales leads):

Proposal (initial):
- 150k tokens of evaluation credits applied to your Brightly test project (valid through June 30).
- A one-time trial window extension until June 5 for the evaluation environment.
- Credits are for benchmarking/eval only and cannot be used for production workloads; usage will be monitored.
- We can provide a short credit memo and a one-page addendum that procurement can attach to the RFP.

Conditions / asks from Brightly:
- Please confirm the primary test team and the email(s) that should receive the credits.
- If Brightly selects Redwood for production within 60 days of the evaluation completion, we can convert up to 50k of the evaluation credits into onboarding credits under the initial contract.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm budget/approval and whether we want to add a small incentive for a 30-day signature? I’ve attached a draft credit memo and the RFP summary we discussed.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@brightlyhealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-10T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightly RFP bake-off — request for evaluation credits and timing

+1 to Neha’s plan. A couple of small tweaks from a deal ops perspective:
- Let’s set the initial credit at 125k tokens and hold 25k as a top-up that we can release after a short benchmarking checkpoint (gives us a bit of protection).
- Add a $2k sign-by incentive if Brightly executes an MSA within 30 days of the bake-off close.

Karthik — if finance is good with staging the credits, I’ll authorize the release. Asha — this staging approach means SRE gets everything needed for the first pass and we keep a small reserve in case you need longer baseline runs.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightly RFP bake-off — request for evaluation credits and timing

Thanks — I’m fine with the staging approach provided we have:
- Budget center: SALES-EVAL-2028 (please confirm GL code before release)
- A short procurement-friendly memo that states credits are non-refundable and for evaluation only.
- Legal to confirm the addendum doesn’t create any open financial commitments.

I’ll approve 125k initial + 25k top-up. Sean — can you confirm the operational steps to apply staged credits to the Brightly project and whether we can time the top-up release to a successful benchmark run (pass/fail criteria)?

Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@brightlyhealth.com>, procurement@brightlyhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T14:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightly RFP bake-off — request for evaluation credits and timing

Asha, procurement team — thank you for the quick responses. Per internal approvals, here is the agreed structure we can offer Brightly for the RFP bake-off:

Offer summary:
- 125,000 tokens applied to the project on May 15 (initial allocation).
- 25,000 token top-up held in reserve; to be released after Brightly completes the baseline benchmark run and shares results (criteria: 99th pct latency test and 10k prompt set pass).
- Trial access extended to June 5 for additional SRE testing; full evaluation credits expire June 30.
- $2,000 performance incentive credit if Brightly signs the MSA within 30 days after evaluation ends.
- We will provide a one-page credit memo and an evaluation addendum for procurement.

Attachments: 20280509_Brightly_eval_credit_memo.pdf (credit memo), Brightly_RFP_summary.xlsx (bake-off test plan).

Next steps:
1) Procurement — please confirm the contact that will accept the credit memo and provide GL code to Redwood.
2) Asha / SRE — confirm the list of test users to provision access (emails).
3) We’ll schedule the initial token allocation for May 15 once we have the above.

Looking forward — and happy to jump on a quick call if you’d like to walk through the pass/fail criteria for the top-up.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: 20280509_Brightly_eval_credit_memo.pdf
